phase: Phase 2 - Unit tests for rho/G/T on real (not synthetic) preprocessed volumes
objective: Do rho/G/T hold on real preprocessed volumes, at the real target scale (grid_shape=8x8x8, 512 tokens), not just synthetic 64-token CI input?

checks.sampling: 12 cases per dataset, seeded random sample (seed=0) from Gate-1 QC-passed manifest rows, stratified across splits present in the sample

decision_rule: PASS iff all sampled real cases pass every Gate-0-equivalent check (formalization Section 12, falsification gates 1 and 4-5), at the real 128^3/512-token scale
interpretation: All 36 sampled real cases (12 per dataset, seeded sample from the frozen Gate-1 manifest) pass every check: rho is numerically PSD and trace-1, G has zero orphan nodes and is a single connected component, T's real gudhi-computed persistence summary is finite, and psi/z contain no NaN/Inf. This is the first time the architecture has run at the real target scale (grid_shape=8x8x8, 512 tokens, matching actual 128^3 materialized volumes) rather than Gate 0's smaller 64-token synthetic-CI scale — validated as parameter-count-equivalent by construction (every DiracModel layer is per-token or fixed-kernel: conv, linear, GCN, transformer all have N-independent parameter counts, confirmed during Phase 0b's own positional-encoding fix, which specifically removed the one N-dependent parameter source — ViT3DBaseline's old learned positional embedding). No real-data edge case (degenerate/near-empty region, HU-normalization outlier, malformed volume) broke any check across all three datasets. One real operational finding, not a correctness bug: per-case latency reading from the mounted bucket was far higher than the pure-compute cost measured in a local smoke test (0.14s/case on synthetic data vs. roughly 100-150s/case observed in this run, total 8939s for 36 cases) - almost certainly bucket-mount read overhead, not model compute. Not a blocker for Gate 2's PASS (correctness, not speed, is what this gate tests), but worth addressing (e.g. batched/parallel reads, or a local scratch cache) before Phase 3 needs to iterate over the full 801-case dataset repeatedly during actual pretraining.
next: Phase 3: pretraining (smoke-scale run first, per IMPLEMENTATION_SPEC.md Phase 3, then the full run pending separate human authorization of that compute spend)
